newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi shares close higher in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: Delhi shares close higher in thin trade.

text.p: Share prices on the Delhi bourse reversed early trends to close higher on Thursday as foreign institutional investors (FIIs) made purchases in the select index-weighted shares, brokers said.
The Delhi Stock Exchange's sensitive index ended 1.90 points higher at 746.35. The index was down 0.08 points after the first 30 minutes of trade.
Brokers said the trading was confined to only a few counters as major players stayed on the sidelines.
"There were very few participants in the market and only the FIIs made some purchases while domestic financial houses remained quiet," said one broker.
Brokers said they were expecting the government to announce a market-friendly budget with measures to boost the capital markets.
Finance Minister P. Chidambaram is expected to present the fiscal budget 1997/98 (April-March) on February 28.
"There is a feeling of pre-budget hesitancy and major players refrained from doing any worthwhile activity for the time being," said Bharat Bhushan of brokers Nu-Era Equity.
Reliance Industries closed a shade higher, up 0.05 rupees, to 272.50 on speculative buying, brokers said.
State Bank of India moved both ways before closing 0.25 rupees lower at 278.35.
Colgate Palmolive rose 3.40 rupees to 274.50 on fresh buying by FIIs.
Hindustan Lever edged 0.90 rupees higher to 907.90.
